national_indicator_definition: The indicator measures the share of the population of Bosnia and Herzegovina aged 18 to 24 with at most lower secondary education who were not involved in any formal or non-formal education or training during the four weeks preceding the survey. The indicator enables monitoring of the prevalence of early leaving from education and training among young people.
national_rationale: The data source is the Agency for Statistics of Bosnia and Herzegovina (BHAS). Data are collected through the Labour Force Survey, and the indicator is calculated as the share of persons aged 18 to 24 with at most lower secondary education who did not participate in formal or non-formal education or training during the four weeks preceding the survey. Educational attainment is classified according to the International Standard Classification of Education (ISCED). Data are expressed as percentages. Progress is calculated automatically based on changes in the indicator values over time. Since a reduction in the share of early leavers from education and training is the desired direction, a decrease in the indicator value represents progress, while an increase represents deterioration. The displayed progress status reflects the trend in the indicator and does not constitute an assessment against a formally established national target.
national_methodology_characteristics: The indicator covers persons aged 18 to 24 with at most lower secondary education who did not participate in formal or non-formal education or training during the four weeks preceding the survey. Data are collected through the Labour Force Survey and enable monitoring of changes over time. Methodological comparability with EU data is based on the use of a common indicator definition and harmonised educational classifications.
national_long_objective: A specific national numerical target for this indicator has not been explicitly established in the strategic documents of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Within the framework of the EU integration and alignment process, Bosnia and Herzegovina monitors this indicator with reference to the EU target of reducing the share of early leavers from education and training to below 9% by 2030. This target serves as an EU reference framework and does not constitute a formally established national target for Bosnia and Herzegovina.
eu_indicator_definition: The indicator measures the share of the population aged 18 to 24 with at most lower secondary education who were not involved in any formal or non-formal education or training during the four weeks preceding the survey. The indicator monitors the prevalence of early leaving from education and training among young people.
eu_rationale: The data source is the European Statistical System (ESS), through the European Union Labour Force Survey (EU-LFS). Data are collected annually and expressed as a percentage of the population aged 18 to 24. Educational attainment is classified according to the International Standard Classification of Education (ISCED). For data from 2014 onwards, lower secondary education covers ISCED levels 0–2 according to ISCED 2011.
eu_methodology_characteristics: The indicator covers persons aged 18 to 24 who have attained at most lower secondary education and who did not participate in formal or non-formal education or training during the four weeks preceding the survey. Data are comparable across EU Member States and other countries covered by the survey, taking into account methodological changes and breaks in time series. Data are published annually.
eu_long_objective: Reducing early leaving from education and training is one of the priorities of European cooperation in education and training. The Council Resolution on a strategic framework for European cooperation in education and training for the period 2021–2030 sets the target of reducing the share of early leavers from education and training to below 9% by 2030. The indicator is also included in the Social Scoreboard of the European Pillar of Social Rights. The long-term reference objective of 4% is used for European performance comparisons and is not the target set by the Council Resolution for 2030.
